description: planner package is part of the root uv workspace and imports successfully
steps: Add planner to the root uv workspace members alongside tool_index
Run uv run --package planner python -c 'import planner; print(planner.__name__)' from the repo root
Verify the import succeeds without touching code under tool_index/

description: Core planner models round-trip through dict persistence, with immutable plan versions and mutable run state
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Create GoalSpec, PlanStep, PlanVersion, RunState, WorldStateSnapshot, StateDelta, FeedbackEvent, ArtifactRef, ContextSnapshot, and EvalResult dataclasses
Implement to_dict/from_dict round-trips for persisted models
Make PlanVersion and PlanStep immutable while keeping RunState mutable for lifecycle updates
Verify a serialized run reloads with the same active_version, world_state, and observed_state_deltas
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue depends on carrying observations forward across planning turns, which requires persisted state objects rather than only prompt text
1::2::RAP frames reasoning as planning over explicit world states, so the runtime needs typed state snapshots and state deltas
2::2::Keeping plan versions immutable while run state remains mutable preserves a clean separation between proposed strategy and observed execution

description: A deterministic bootstrap planning policy decomposes a complex user query into ordered, dependency-aware plan steps
papers: 1:Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents (arXiv 2201.07207)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Interpret the raw query into GoalSpec with objective, constraints, success criteria, and ambiguity notes
Split multi-part requests into sequential PlanStep objects with explicit dependencies
Infer a coarse step kind per subtask: reason, retrieve, tool, validate, or synthesize
Verify a query like 'research two vendors, compare tradeoffs, then draft a recommendation' yields multiple ordered steps plus a final validation step
refers: 0::0::Zero-Shot Planners shows that high-level language goals can be expanded into actionable subgoals; this task makes that decomposition explicit in code
1::2::RAP treats intermediate reasoning states as part of the planning process, so the output plan needs dependency structure instead of a flat checklist
2::2::A bootstrap planner gives the runtime a stable initial graph before any search or feedback-driven revision happens

description: Abstract plan steps can be grounded onto admissible capability identifiers through a registry-backed action grounder
papers: 1:Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents (arXiv 2201.07207)
steps: Define CapabilitySpec and GroundedAction models for the executable action layer
Implement a registry-backed ActionGrounder that scores capability matches from step title, instructions, and capability_hint
Prefer an exact capability_hint match when one exists, otherwise fall back to token overlap scoring
Verify a search-oriented step grounds to web_search and an unmatched step returns no admissible action
refers: 0::0::Zero-Shot Planners separates semantic planning from mapping a plan onto valid environment actions
1::0::The paper's planner is only useful after actions are translated into the environment's admissible action space, which is why capability IDs are first-class here

description: A file-backed planner store persists goals, plan versions, run state, artifacts, and feedback logs by run_id
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Persist goal.json, state.json, plans/vN.json, artifacts/<id>.json, and feedback/events.jsonl under a per-run directory
Implement load helpers that reconstruct typed models from disk
Ensure list_plan_versions returns sorted plan versions for the run
Verify artifacts and feedback can be reloaded after a fresh store instance is created
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue improves later reasoning by feeding back observations from earlier actions, which requires durable feedback storage
1::2::RAP models reasoning as transitions across state trajectories, so persisted world state and plan history are core runtime data, not optional logs

description: PlannerRuntime manages step readiness, execution state, failure state, and grounded actions during a run
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Implement PlannerRuntime.start_run to create GoalSpec, PlanVersion v1, and an initial RunState
Expose next_ready_steps so only dependency-satisfied steps move from pending to ready
Implement transitions for ready to running to done and ready to running to failed
Record grounded capability IDs for executable steps inside the active run state
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue alternates plan, act, observe, and revise, which maps naturally to an explicit step lifecycle
1::2::RAP explores state transitions rather than one-shot outputs, so the runtime needs machine-readable step status changes

description: Context assembly builds a focused per-step snapshot from goal, active plan, current world state, recent artifacts, and open questions
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Build ContextSnapshot for a target step using the active GoalSpec and PlanVersion
Include current world state, recent artifacts, open questions, completed summaries, and grounded actions
Limit context to relevant or recent artifacts instead of replaying the entire run history
Verify unrelated historical artifacts are omitted when artifact_limit is smaller than total artifacts
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue conditions later reasoning on current observations, not on a full transcript replay of every previous token
1::2::RAP's world-model framing means the next decision should depend on the current state snapshot and candidate future actions, which makes selective context assembly important

description: Feedback events update observed world state, record open questions, and persist the observation trail for later replanning
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Implement record_feedback with source, summary, observed_state_delta, success flag, and new open questions
Apply observed_state_delta to the run's WorldStateSnapshot and increment its revision
Append feedback events to the per-run feedback log and track their IDs in RunState
Verify a failed observation can add a new open question without completing the underlying step
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue's core insight is that new observations should feed directly back into the next reasoning turn
1::2::RAP depends on explicit state transitions, so observed deltas must update the runtime's world state rather than living only in free-form notes

description: Replanning creates a new immutable plan version with parent linkage while preserving prior plan history and carried-forward completed work
papers: 2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Implement PlannerRuntime.replan to write PlanVersion v2+ with parent_version pointing at the previously active plan
Switch RunState.active_version to the new plan while keeping prior plan files intact
Carry forward completed or reusable step status when a step ID is intentionally reused in the new version
Verify v1 and v2 are both loadable after replanning and that only active_version changes in the mutable run state
refers: 0::1::Inner Monologue shows that new observations can force plan revision; immutable versions preserve that revision trail for debugging and auditability
1::2::RAP reasons over alternative futures, so the runtime should supersede the active plan without overwriting previous trajectories

description: A bounded best-first search policy explores branching plan continuations and returns the highest-scoring path within an expansion budget
papers: 3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
steps: Define SearchNode and SearchResult for search-time state tracking
Implement a bounded best-first SearchPolicy with max_expansions and beam_width controls
Reconstruct the best path from parent pointers after search completes
Verify the policy chooses the higher-reward branch on a small synthetic state graph and stops at the configured expansion budget
refers: 0::2::RAP explicitly reframes reasoning as planning with a world model and uses search over future states instead of a single greedy rollout
1::2::A bounded best-first policy provides the same explicit branching hook while staying simpler than full MCTS for v1

description: An optional symbolic subplanner protocol handles deterministic subtasks that benefit from a formal solver path
papers: 4:LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency (arXiv 2304.11477)
steps: Define a SymbolicSubplanner protocol whose solve method returns an ordered action sequence for a deterministic subgoal
Provide a mock symbolic solver implementation for tests
Allow runtime or policy code to call the symbolic path only when a subtask is marked deterministic
Verify the mocked solver returns a stable sequence for the same deterministic goal text
refers: 0::3::LLM+P improves planning reliability by handing formalizable subproblems to a classical planner instead of relying on free-form generation alone
1::3::Keeping the symbolic path optional matches the paper's hybrid framing: use formal planning where it helps, not for every step

description: An objective evaluator checks dependency validity, executable-step feasibility, and expected-versus-observed state transitions
papers: 5:PlanBench: An Extensible Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Planning and Reasoning about Change (arXiv 2206.10498)
steps: Reject plans with missing dependencies or dependency cycles
Flag executable tool steps that are not grounded onto an admissible capability
Compare expected_state_delta from the plan against observed_state_deltas from execution and report mismatches
Return EvalResult with passed, score, issues, and structured details
refers: 0::4::PlanBench focuses on objective plan correctness and reasoning about change, so evaluation should inspect explicit plan structure and state transitions
1::4::State-consistency checks are a direct response to the benchmark's emphasis on whether actions produce the world changes the plan assumes

description: Integration test runs a complex multi-part session through planning, grounding, execution updates, feedback, replanning, search, and evaluation
papers: 1:Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents (arXiv 2201.07207)
2:Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (arXiv 2207.05608)
3:Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP, arXiv 2305.14992)
4:LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency (arXiv 2304.11477)
5:PlanBench: An Extensible Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Planning and Reasoning about Change (arXiv 2206.10498)
steps: Start a run from a complex query that includes retrieval, comparison, and final writing subtasks
Ground the executable steps, complete at least one step with an artifact and observed state delta, and record feedback that introduces a new open question
Trigger a replan that creates v2 while preserving v1 and carrying forward reusable completed work
Run bounded search over a small branching decision, optionally call the mock symbolic subplanner for a deterministic subgoal, and finalize the run after objective evaluation passes
refers: 0::0::Zero-Shot Planners motivates the initial decomposition of a complex request into actionable subtasks
1::1::Inner Monologue motivates feeding observations back into the next planning turn and revising the plan when the world changes
2::2::RAP motivates explicit state updates and bounded search over alternative futures during the same session
3::3::LLM+P motivates retaining a symbolic hook for deterministic subproblems inside an otherwise language-driven planner
4::4::PlanBench motivates ending the session only after a structural and state-transition validity check passes
